SBMT 1100.title: Business Study Trip
SBMT 1100.description: This course is offered in the form of a study trip to another country in the winter and summer term.  Each study trip will consist of at least three elements, namely lectures delivered by faculty members at the host institution, company visits and cultural adventure in the host country.  Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course.  Graded P or F.
cilos: Demonstrate cultural awareness and adaptability by actively participating in cultural adventures, showcasing the ability to engage with diverse environments and practices.

Apply knowledge gained from study trip activites to critically analyze real-world business operations and strategies in the host country, fostering an understanding of practical applications in a global context.

Reflect on the overall experience of the study trip, integrating insights from trip activities, including but not limited to lectures, company visits, and cultural interactions to articulate a comprehensive understanding of international business dynamics.

SBMT 1111.title: Business Student Induction
SBMT 1111.description: This is an induction course designed for all new students in the School of Business and Management. Students will be divided into 10 cohorts and assigned to designated academic advisors. They will also be participating in a series of planned activities, aiming to help them build bonds and simultaneously identify personal academic interest, examine educational goals, and develop plans to meet objectives through academic advising and other personal development workshops and programs. Graded P or F.

SBMT 2100-2110.title: Community Services Project
SBMT 2100-2110.description: This course is offered in a form of a community project at a designated non-governmental organization (NGO) under the supervision of the School. Students are required to attend all the training sessions, design and implement the service project or participate in the service learning tasks as instructed by the host NGO and/or the course instructors. By the end of the course, students have to submit a reflective statement in the format of a paper, a group project report or a presentation to demonstrate the attainment of all intended learning outcomes, in addition to other requirements of the relevant NGO as appropriate. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded PP, P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.
cilos: Gain and apply solid working experience at a real workplace, engaging with the front stage and backstage of the service, and understand the society from a social good perspective.
Understand the society from a social good perspective.

Apply skills to real-world challenges, applying expertise in areas such as project management, research, advocacy, fundraising, communications, or any other relevant field to contribute to the organization's mission and goals.

Explore the careers in NGOs and SE, gaining experience in different roles, departments, or even different organizations within the sector. The goal is to broaden knowledge, gain exposure, and identify areas of interest and expertise.
Facilitate personal growth, engaging in activities that foster personal growth, resilience, and self-awareness.

SBMT 2200.title: Social Enterprise Internship Program
SBMT 2200.description: The course is intended to give business undergraduate students an opportunity to gain exposure in the area of social entrepreneurship and apply their knowledge to solve real-world challenges facing these organizations. It is conducted in the form of an internship program at a designated social enterprise under the supervision of the School of Business and Management. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.
cilos: Analyze basic organizational and the Project Partner issues from both internal and external perspectives.
Participate interactively in team discussions and decision-making.
Present essential findings in both written and oral form to a variety of stakeholders in the project.
Applies concepts, knowledge, skills and methodologies learned from business courses to specific, real-world business problems and issues.

SBMT 2800.title: SBM Cooperative Education Program
SBMT 2800.description: This course is intended to enhance SBM students’ career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For SBM Year 2 students or above only. Graded P, PP or F.
cilos: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

SBMT 2800.title: SBM Cooperative Education Program
SBMT 2800.description: This course is intended to enhance SBM students’ career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For SBM Year 2 students or above only. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

SBMT 2900.title: Special Topics in Business and Management
SBMT 2900.description: Special topics in an identified area of Business and Management; topics vary with instructor.  May be graded P or F.
cilos: (Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

SBMT 3100.title: Business Field Study Fundamentals
SBMT 3100.description: The course is mostly a supervised study of a real-life issue faced by an organization.  Students will be given opportunities to support organization's effort through assisting in collection and analysis of data, identification of strategic questions, design of studies, development and reporting.  At the end of the course, students will be given a taste of real-life business experience.  Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course.  May be Graded DI/PA/F.

SBMT 3200-3210.title: Corporate Project
SBMT 3200-3210.description: Students apply skills and knowledge learned from business courses to focus on specific projects in a corporation setting. Students will work on group projects sponsored by participating corporations and supervised by faculty members. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded PP, P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different topics are taken.
cilos: Apply the business knowledge and innovative approaches to real-world business problems.
Serve as student consultants and provide solutions to business issues faced by corporate partners.
Participate interactively in team discussions and decision-making.
Present essential findings in both written and oral form to a variety of stakeholders in the project.

SBMT 3300.title: Business Competitions
SBMT 3300.description: In each business competition, students will be required to examine the conceptual and practical aspects of business policies and policy decision making by utilizing all the concepts, theories and tools that they learned in previous courses. This 1-credit course is offered in recognition of the students' outstanding performance in their participation of business competitions. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. Graded P or F. Students may repeat the course for credits if different case competitions are taken.
cilos: Acquire effective techniques for interpersonal communication and teamwork in addition to real life opportunities and experience of thinking-on-your-feet.
Simulates the urgency, complexity, and uncertainty prevalent in "real-world" business organizations.

SBMT 4000.title: SBM Undergraduate Honors Research Project
SBMT 4000.description: The two‐term SBM Undergraduate Honors Research Project is for SBM students who are interested in pursuing systematic research at the senior undergraduate level. The course will act as a pre‐doctoral training program to help students expand their options in seeking future doctoral study opportunities. Students are expected to research a focused problem under close supervision by a faculty and produce a thesis after completing this course. For SBM students in their final year of study only. Approval from the course coordinator is needed prior to enrolling in the course. May be graded PP.
cilos: Describe the process of academic research in a selected business discipline.
Describe, compare, and contrast different research methodologies.
Analyze the contextual features leading to particular individual, organizational, or social outcomes in a chosen business setting and problem.
Apply or adapt appropriate research methodology to study the chosen problem.
Develop a research paper with scope and quality commensurate with a top conference paper in the selected business discipline.
Present the research to an expert panel.

SBMT 5010.title: Accounting for Managers
SBMT 5010.description: The first part of the course provides students with a basic foundation and practical understanding of financial accounting.  Focus is on the design, use and impact of financial information and accounting measures in organizational planning and control.  The second part of the course is to apply and analyze accounting information in managerial decision making with the fundamental concepts of accrual accounting given in the first part.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.
cilos: Comprehensively explain major principles governing financial and managerial accounting.
Develop analytical and basic technical skills required to prepare financial accounting records and reports, as well as to use and interpret them.
Identify the role of managerial accounting in decision-making process of managers in business organizations.
Form critical judgement by identifying and defining accounting and business problems, applying analytical and quantitative techniques, and making and justifying decision.

SBMT 5020.title: Fundamentals of Economics and Finance
SBMT 5020.description: The first part of the course covers managerial economics: understanding of economics and the application of economic analysis in the context of the needs of management and of managerial decision-making in today's changing environment.  The second part of the course covers the basic concepts in finance.  Topics include time value of money, valuation of securities, capital budgeting including computation of cash flows, NPV, IRR, portfolio theory and capital asset pricing model, and rudimentary concepts about options and futures contracts.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.
cilos: Identify basic Microeconomic theories such as consumer theory, firms' optimal decision making under different contexts, and the operation and properties of perfectly competitive markets.
Recognize the Economics methodology and apply economic analysis in managerial decision making.

SBMT 5030.title: Marketing Management and Strategy
SBMT 5030.description: The first part of this module covers marketing management using the framework of the 4P's (Product, Price, Promotion and Place).  Topics include consumer needs and wants, marketing research, advertising and sales promotion, pricing theory, etc.  The impact of the Internet on all aspects of marketing will also be examined.  The second part will cover marketing and business policy from a strategic perspective.  Decision making in a competitive environment in the face of environmental constraints will also be examined.  Registration is limited to students on the MSc program in Engineering Enterprise Management only.
cilos: Conduct a marketing environmental analysis and identify market opportunities that will be strategically fit with the company or organization.
Identify and evaluate segments, and decide on the appropriate target(s) within a given market.
Construct a persuasive value proposition and positioning statement for a given offering.
Formulate marketing strategies and make strategic marketing decisions, including specific marketing mix strategies.
Monitor and control strategic marketing plans.
Make effective presentations of a company’s or organization’s marketing plan.

SBMT 5040.title: Applied Statistics in Business Intelligence for Decision Making/ Business Forecasting
SBMT 5040.description: Applied Statistics is a tool that can be used in a variety of business settings, but despite the widespread discussion of terms like Business Intelligence, the truth is that these areas are actually not very well understood. Advances in computing power can now give businesses ways to analyze data that they never could before. This course examines with these advances, how firms can make decisions about pricing, marketing, new products, and resource allocation more effectively than they have ever been able to in the past. Graded P or F.
cilos: Define statistical concepts.
Explain the use of statistical tools in a business setting.
Exemplify the broad applications of business intelligence.
Explain in general terms what steps firms need to take to implement business intelligence.
Identify areas where business intelligence can alter the way a company conducts operations.

SBMT 5050.title: ESG Investing and Green Finance Strategy for Portfolio Management
SBMT 5050.description: This course examines the different frameworks for incorporating environmental, social and governance (ESG) and responsible investing practices from both the investor and corporate boardroom perspectives. The various approaches to ESG investing, including ESG inclusion, ESG integration, ESG engagement and ESG screening will be covered comprehensively. The full spectrum of ESG products and strategies across the equity and fixed income asset classes will be covered.
cilos: Understand different frameworks for incorporating ESG and responsible investing practices from both the investor and corporate boardroom perspectives.
Master the various approaches to ESG investing, including ESG inclusion, integration, engagement and screening.
Familiarize with full spectrum of ESG products and strategies across the equity and fixed income asset classes.
Acknowledge traps and pitfalls in implementing an ESG strategy via case study of practical ESG investing application.
Understand carbon pricing and trading.

SBMT 5060.title: Creativity and Innovation in Marketing
SBMT 5060.description: This course will cover several systematic creative problem-solving methodologies which are appropriately implemented when a decision has been made to search for a creative solution. Apart from focusing on new product ideation and creative marketing actions, it offers skills to learn how to solve problems, identify opportunities, and generate those elusive ideas that potentially generate benefits to organizations.
cilos: Master systematic creative problem-solving methodologies and its implementation.
Solve problems, identify opportunities, and generate those elusive ideas that potentially generate benefits to organizations.
Understand product ideation and creative marketing actions.
Identify and resolve communications dilemma.

SBMT 5070.title: Sustainability Applications in the Corporate World
SBMT 5070.description: Sustainability is a topic of increasing focus for public and private companies around the world. With global environmental and other societal challenges increasing, and with increasing interest anticipated, trillions of dollars in market share are beginning to shift. This battle for future market share may well be won by those who respond best to this new corporate, policy and investment paradigm. This course provides students with the experience, tools and community of practice they will need to become an important part of this global paradigm. Graded P or F.
cilos: Understand real-world applications of sustainability.
Develop responses to Environmental, Social and Governance challenges.
Analyze short-term profitability versus long-term sustainability and tradeoffs.

SBMT 5080.title: C-suite Life
SBMT 5080.description: The course aims to provide a simulated and role-play environment to enable students to apply their MBA learnings and experience in a complex management world. C-Suite Life is a real-time, live case study that covers a broad range of business challenges spanning the field of management. Full engagement from students is expected.
cilos: Analyze the crisis with managerial insight and instinct.
Generate well-structured solutions, actions, and responses timely when a crisis occurs.
Apply theory and practice for effective decision-making.
Develop a crisis management team.

SBMT 5300.title: Enhancing Professional Skills
SBMT 5300.description: It aims at helping MBA students work intensively on developing or improving some key presentation skills which will be useful to them throughout their business careers. Simply put, the essence of Enhancing Professional Skills as “Making a Logical, Effective and Persuasive Business Presentation". Graded P or F.
cilos: Identify the key issues from a tangle of issues, to analyze and develop solutions.
Create and deliver logical, effective and persuasive business presentations.
Enhance communication effectiveness.

SBMT 5460.title: Business Plans Competition
SBMT 5460.description: The objective of this course is to provide hands on perspective of what it takes to start a successful business from the business plan, to funding, to beginning operations.  Students will go overseas to participate in international business plan competitions.  Graded P or F.
cilos: Create ideas and formulate feasible strategies for startups or venture at early growth stage.
Develop and deliver persuasive business presentations.
Integrate and apply the knowledge learnt in business operation.
Increase exposure  in a global business context.

SBMT 5470.title: Case Analysis Competition
SBMT 5470.description: The objective of this course is to provide hands on perspective of what it takes to analyze a real-life business case.  Students will go overseas to participant in international case competitions.  Graded P or F.
cilos: Analyse a relevant  current case.
Evaluate various business solutions.
Develop and prepare a convincing presentation.
Increase exposure  in a global business context.

SBMT 5715.title: AI, Innovation, and Product Management
SBMT 5715.description: This course provides the basic principles and tools that business managers need to ensure outcomes align with business needs. Students will gain an industry insider’s view that goes beyond theory to cover actionable guidelines, practical tips, and best practices. By examining the differing modes of product development in Silicon Valley and China, this course provides a new framework and approach for competition and innovation in the Age of AI. Graded P or F.
cilos: Explain the basic concepts, use cases, applications, and limitations of artificial intelligence.
Apply the skills to leverage AI to capture market opportunities and address operational needs.
Explain the basic methodology, tools, and concepts of product management, including how to build AI into a company’s products and services.
Develop product strategy at both the corporate and startup level.
Differentiate the different modes of innovation and AI between the East and West.

SBMT 5720.title: MBA Accelerator - Accounting
SBMT 5720.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in financial accounting, managerial accounting and finance to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. The course will also cover the basic business concepts, financial statement analysis, cost classifications and how to do managerial decisions. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply fundamental knowledge in both financial and managerial accounting.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in knowledge level among students from different background to assist smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of techniques and skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Evaluate cost-volume-profit analysis and apply core managerial accounting information to strategic decision making.

SBMT 5730.title: MBA Accelerator - Python
SBMT 5730.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in technical skills to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. Python is used for creating high-level abstractions for well-written and well-optimized frameworks, where business applications rely on. The course will cover Python programming language for developing business applications, the practical libraries and packages. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply fundamental knowledge in business programming and Python syntax.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in technical knowledge level among students from different background to assist  smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of techniques and skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Design and debug Python programs.
Develop business applications with Python.

SBMT 5740.title: MBA Accelerator - Data Analysis
SBMT 5740.description: This pre-program course aims to provide elementary or refreshing knowledge in quantitative and analysis hard skills to prepare students for the academic demands and rigor of MBA courses. It will cover data and variation, probability model and association between random variables at introductory level. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply fundamental knowledge in quantitative skills and statistics analysis.
Generate a better sense of MBA learning momentum and minimize the gap in knowledge level among students from different background to assist smooth transition to learning.
Recognize the level of statistics and hard skills required for accomplishing the study plan ahead.
Recognize and describe statistical methods typically used in the analysis of business data.

SBMT 5755.title: Fundamental Value Investing: Applications to Public and Private Equity
SBMT 5755.description: This course covers value investing from a practitioner’s perspective and is oriented around the value investing framework and process culminating in an interactive presentation to an Investment Committee. Participants will learn key concepts and tools used in value investing, how to analyze and determine what makes a good business, and how to assess intrinsic value.
cilos: Identify and evaluate investment opportunities.
Develop value investment analysis, including analyzing businesses, financial modelling and valuation.
Recognize risks and the due diligence process.
Differentiate the commonalities and differences between value investing in private and public companies.

SBMT 5760.title: Financial and Money Markets from Macroeconomic Perspectives
SBMT 5760.description: The course will discuss the main financial markets, their characteristics and how they are linked to the economy. It starts by explaining how global financial markets are structured and how this structure services both borrowers and investors. Asset classes for investor funds are reviewed before the focus turns to the macroeconomic environment. Fixed income, equities, commodities and real estate are also covered in detail and students will explore how hedge funds and private equity firms create value for their stakeholders.
cilos: Analyze the impacts from the release of economic data.
Compare the key derivative products which are relevant to most major securities markets.
Evaluate time value of money, yield curves, the price/yield relationship and market quoting conventions.
Recognize the process of investing in real estate assets.

SBMT 5770.title: From MBA to Stock Market: Applied Value Investing
SBMT 5770.description: This course will deliver the frameworks and processes of value investing that some of the most successful investors in the world employ to manage and preserve capital. Students will learn to use quantitative valuation techniques, such as asset-based, earning power, and the value of growth, to develop a strategic methodology for estimating a company's franchise value. A number of case studies will be used throughout the program to improve students’ ability to manage a value portfolio. Graded P or F.

SBMT 5780.title: Personal Wealth Management for Working Professionals
SBMT 5780.description: The course aims to focus on several major financial products which are widely traded, but not widely understood, such as stock, foreign exchange, bonds, insurance and other derivatives. Students will learn about managing own personal wealth by using technical analytics skills to breakdown different common investment products and examine the impacts of behavioral psychology in the trading market. The course will also systematically introduce how the macro-economic cycles and megatrends affect businesses and markets. Students will acquire how to identify and analyze the investment opportunities, manage risks and articulate their views in portfolio construction. An overview of common insurance products available in the retail market will be discussed, with an emphasis on finding the right insurance coverage for individual needs, as part of one’s wealth management strategy.
cilos: Execute the portfolio construction.
Recognize the foreign exchange (FX) market, the commonly traded FX derivatives and the reasons for trading them.
Evaluate appropriate insurance package for different individual needs.
Apply technical skills to analyze different investment products.

SBMT 5790.title: Economic Development in Asia: A Practitioner’s Perspective
SBMT 5790.description: This course examines how economic development has occurred in East Asia, emphasizing the importance of land and agricultural reforms, export-led industrialization, financial repression, technology upgrading, and increasing economic complexity. Throughout the course, students will discover growth opportunities for businesses in Asia not only from a corporate strategy and operations perspective but also from an investor’s perspective.
cilos: Recognize the key principles and practices of economic development, focusing on the role of land and agricultural reforms, export-led industrialization, financial repression, technology upgrading, and increasing economic complexity.
Analyze and evaluate contemporary growth and development challenges faced by major Asian economies.
Identify and interpret the implications of growth and development challenges on business opportunities and investment strategies.

SBMT 6010-6090.title: Special Topics
SBMT 6010-6090.description: Selected topics in business and management. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.
cilos: Analyse current hot topics relevant to the business world.
Address the challenges and opportunities from the selected business topics.

SBMT 6100.title: Field Study Project
SBMT 6100.description: This is a supervised study of a real-life issue faced by an organization, including identification of strategic questions, design of studies, collection and analysis of data, development and reporting recommendation. The projects selected should bring a meaningful economic performance impact to the sponsoring companies. May be graded by letter, PP or P/F for different offerings.
cilos: Develop a consulting project effectively.
Combine therotical knowledge and analytical skills to formulate solutions to practical business problems in real world settings.
Organize clear and engaging business presentations for a senior management audience.
Produce professional quality project deliverables including agendas, briefs, proposals, models and reports.

SBMT 6200.title: Independent Study
SBMT 6200.description: Study of selected issues from various departments under the supervision of a faculty member from SBM. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)
cilos: Identify a certain business issue.
Apply the knowledge learnt in tackling real business issue.
Analyse different aspects of the business issue.
Generate feasible, sensible and practial recommendations / solutions.

SBMT 6300-6310.title: Global Study Tour
SBMT 6300-6310.description: The course aims to expand students' horizon and understanding on the social, economic and business context of different cultures. Led by HKUST faculty, the study tour provides students with the opportunity to learn from leading professionals in selected locations globally through visits to partner universities or corporates, as well as meetings with local business leaders or alumni. Course duration will range from one week to multi-weeks. Students are allowed to repeat this course for credit if the locations of the study tours are different. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.
cilos: Advance social, economic and cultural knowledge in a global setting.
Adapt to local business practices to enhance leadership capabilities.
Recognize core concepts of business functions required for global business leaders.
Communicate effectively through oral presentations and paper writing.

SBMT 6320-6330.title: DBi Study Tour
SBMT 6320-6330.description: This course is hosted by partner schools in different countries. The tour gives an overview of doing business, including an introduction to the economy, history, culture and legal framework of the visiting country. Typically, it will include lectures on-campus and off-campus, corporate visits and meeting with local business leaders upon a range of industry sectors which will offer students a unique synthesis between state of the art academic studies and practical, hands-on experience. It is suitable for those who are specifically interested in doing business in the visiting place in future or in international business and enhancing their international experience. Graded P or F.
cilos: Identify implications for the economy and business of different government and tax policies.
Identify the drivers of the economy, economic condition and global position.
Recognize the local market condition and impact of culture on business operation.
Develop top management perspective and design competitive business-level strategies for the industry.
Explain the role of local government policies with respect to international trade.

SBMT 6340.title: Career Trek
SBMT 6340.description: Career Trek is an overseas tour for participants to expand their business horizon and to explore the latest career opportunities in other countries. It mainly involves company visits to give students a practical understanding of day-to-day-operations in different fields of interest through meeting prospective employers to discuss specific jobs and career paths within each organization. Students can expand their networks, learn about the countries’ cultures and understand the hiring landscape in different regions across industries. The duration of the treks will range from several days to a full-week. Students are allowed to repeat this course for credits if the locations of the treks are different. Consent of instructor is required. Graded P or F.
cilos: Analyze the professional culture of the organization they visit and explain how their skills potentially relate to a particular profession.
Identify regional job markets and the best way to successfully find a career in a specific field.
Develop professional connection with organizations and other professionals visited during the trek.
Apply knowledge about the world of work and career development to their lives.

SBMT 6350.title: MBA Practical Internship Experience
SBMT 6350.description: This course is to provide students with practical work experience. Internships provide entry-level, career-related experience, and workplace competencies that employers value when hiring new employees. It is also an opportunity to explore career fields. Students can gain a clearer sense of what they still need to learn and to build professional networks. The experience will enhance students’ knowledge and likelihood of success in post-MBA job search. Course duration and credits depend on the cumulative working hours. Students are allowed to repeat this course for credits if they have more than one internship. Consent of instructor is required. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Generate practical experience, insights and knowledge in a field relevant to their major of studies.
Apply major and academic specific knowledge in a workplace setting.
Develop connections with industry professionals which lead to more job offers.
Acquire technical and soft skills which only come with experience, including skills important for time management, discipline and self-learning.
Execute practically teamwork, effective communication, collaboration and leadership.

SBMT 6360.title: MBA Career Development Program
SBMT 6360.description: The course provides students access to practical and customized learning opportunities to be equipped with knowledge, skills and attributes to further advance in their careers. Workshops and training sessions such as recruitment talks and executive sharing can keep students exposed to valuable career connections, abreast with the latest development in the commercial world and trends in the job market. Through these career development activities, students will get to evaluate their own strengths and weaknesses, identify areas for improvement, collect feedback on interview techniques, further improve and formulate a personalized strategy to develop their career goals. Consent of instructor is required. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Confidently and professionally present themselves to potential employers via their professional resumes and profiles.
Identify resources and collaborators among staff, trainers, alumni, and peers who can help them in their career development process.
Plan their career timeline, options and goal, and accelerate their job search progress.
Analyze one’s career strengths and weaknesses, and essential continuous improvements which drive career growth.

SBMT 6370.title: Global Network Week
SBMT 6370.description: The course aims to integrate global horizons and foster cross-cultural, economic, and social understanding by immersing MBA/MSc students in another culture. Students will have the opportunity to study a short-term program at one of the top business schools of the Global Network for Advanced Management (GNAM) and learn from leading professionals in selected locations globally. Some of the GNAM member schools include INSEAD, HEC Paris, UC Berkeley, LSE, IE Business School, etc. Typically the program will include lectures on-campus and off-campus, corporate visits, and meeting with local business leaders, etc. This course may be repeated for credits if students participate more than once in Global Network Week. Graded P or F.
cilos: Advance social, economic and cultural knowledge in a global setting.
Adapt to local business practices to enhance leadership capabilities.
Integrate learnings of global student peers from partner business schools around the world.

SBMT 6380.title: GNAM Small Network Online Courses
SBMT 6380.description: The Small Network Online Courses (SNOC) enroll a select group of students engaged in a common effort to build management skills. They are offered virtually by a member school of the Global Network for Advanced Management (GNAM), connecting students online for lectures and discussions, and collaborative team projects, developing teamwork skills and cross-cultural perspectives. The course may be repeated for credits if the SNOCs taken are offered by different schools. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Develop international connections with the GNAM member schools’ students.
Recognize the member schools’ counties market condition and impact of culture on business operation.
Apply top management perspective and design competitive business-level strategies for the GNAM member schools’ local industries.
Analyze the first-hand case studies from different countries to investigate the global business problems.

SBMT 6390.title: MSc Practicum
SBMT 6390.description: This course offers MSc students the opportunities to gain hands-on experience through real-world practice. Students apply advanced business concepts to solve practical challenges, enhancing problem-solving, teamwork, and professional skills. The practicum bridges academic learning and industry practice, preparing graduates for impactful careers in a dynamic business environment. Graded P or F.
cilos: Gain practical experience and insights in a field relevant to their area of study.
Apply academic and discipline-specific knowledge effectively in a professional setting.
Build meaningful connections with industry professionals, enhancing career opportunities.
Develop technical and soft skills such as time management, discipline, adaptability, and self-directed learning.
Demonstrate teamwork, communication, collaboration, and leadership in real-world business contexts.

SBMT 6400.title: MSc Study Tour
SBMT 6400.description: This experiential course provides MSc students with an immersive learning opportunity through international or regional study tours. Each tour focuses on either a specific industry or a particular geographic region, enabling students to gain a comprehensive understanding of the job market and emerging career opportunities. During the tour, students will engage with industry leaders, cultural institutions, and academic partners to acquire practical insights and broaden their global business perspectives. Graded P or F.
cilos: Analyze global business practices within diverse cultural, economic and industry contexts.
Apply theoretical knowledge to real-world business scenarios.
Demonstrate intercultural communication and professional networking skills.
Reflect on personal and professional development gained through experiential learning.

SBMT 6780.title: Professional Development in Ethics, Innovation and Technology for Research Postgraduate Students
SBMT 6780.description: This one-credit course is intended to provide basic professional training to research postgraduate students in the School of Business and Management. The course will begin with lectures and a workshop on ethics in research, which is designed to enable students to keep abreast of current issues in research and trends within the corporate, private and government sectors, as it relates to the impact and usage of technology. Students will be provided with the opportunities to interact with individuals in the corporate sector to engage in discourse of a practical nature. The mode of delivery will consist of lectures given by faculty and/ or guest speakers, students reading groups, discipline-specific workshops on various topics. Graded  PP, P or F.
cilos: Explain ethical issues in regards to research for human subjects.
